headline: Semis and Power Names Lead Broad Friday Rally as Oil Shock Looms Over the Week Ahead
body_html:
Markets closed Friday's session on firm footing, with 396 of 545 names in our universe advancing — a nearly three-to-one beat on breadth. Semiconductors were the standout, adding 3.15% as a cohort, while Homebuilders rose 1.58% and Industrials gained 1.24%. Healthcare was the lone sector to finish in the red, dipping a marginal 0.01%. Power-adjacent names dominated the leaderboard: Vicor Corporation surged 11.15%, Forgent Power Solutions jumped 8.97%, and ON Semiconductor climbed 8.51%, signaling renewed conviction around electrification and data-center power infrastructure.

The week ahead arrives shadowed by an escalating energy crisis. Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline after drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory, Houthi forces have reached a strategically critical Red Sea island, and crude has completed a roundtrip to the $100 per barrel threshold. President Trump has pointed to Iran as the likely architect of the pipeline attack. Any further escalation could jolt energy and materials markets sharply, adding volatility to what is already a geopolitically charged backdrop.

On the political calendar, election officials have moved to restrict certain public employees from trading on prediction markets ahead of November's midterms — a development worth monitoring for regulatory ripple effects. Meanwhile, investors will be watching whether last week's semiconductor momentum can hold as macro headlines compete for attention and hedges on oil-supply risk build into the open.

briefs.headline: Houthi Advance Puts Red Sea Shipping and Gulf Oil Supplies in the Crosshairs
briefs.body: Houthi forces have seized a key island position in the Red Sea while simultaneously intensifying pressure on Gulf shipping lanes. Saudi Arabia confirmed drone strikes hit its East-West pipeline, prompting a temporary shutdown. Riyadh has so far held off on retaliation, but markets are pricing in rising supply-disruption risk as crude hovers near $100.

briefs.headline: Iraq Dismisses Military Commander Amid Saudi Pipeline Fallout
briefs.body: Baghdad moved swiftly to terminate a senior military officer following drone attacks originating from Iraqi soil that struck Saudi energy infrastructure. Separately, Iraq ordered the closure of its Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran. The twin actions signal Baghdad is attempting to contain diplomatic damage as regional tensions spike.

briefs.headline: BRICS Declaration Tests Alliance Cohesion Against Mideast Fault Lines
briefs.body: Member nations of the BRICS grouping reached a joint declaration over the weekend, according to Reuters, even as Middle East tensions threatened to expose divisions within the bloc. The agreement is being read as a signal that economic coordination among major emerging economies can survive geopolitical friction — at least for now.

briefs.headline: Power-Module and Storage Hardware Names Electrify Friday's Leaderboard
briefs.body: Beyond the semiconductor sector's broad 3.15% gain, individual standouts underscored a clear thematic thread: power delivery and data infrastructure. Vicor Corporation added 11.15%, NetApp climbed 8.54%, and IT reseller CDW Corp rose 7.85%, suggesting institutional rotation into names tied to AI-driven infrastructure build-out.

briefs.headline: Metallurgical Coal Stocks Slide as Risk-Off Currents Hit Materials
briefs.body: Alpha Metallurgical Resources and Warrior Met Coal each fell 3.82% on Friday, making the met-coal patch the weakest corner of an otherwise resilient Materials sector — which itself gained only 0.18% on the day. Softening steel demand signals and elevated geopolitical uncertainty weighed on the group heading into the weekend.

briefs.headline: J&J's Surgical Robotics Push Puts Healthcare Innovation Back in Focus
briefs.body: Johnson & Johnson's Ottava surgical robot is drawing analyst attention as the healthcare giant moves to capture a growing slice of the robotic-assisted surgery market. The development stands in contrast to Healthcare's marginal underperformance on Friday — down 0.01% — and may offer a longer-term catalyst for the sector heading into the fall earnings season.
